properties.description:
HLSLCH

This product covers Southwest Louisiana and Southeast Texas

EDOUARD WEAKENING...DOWNGRADED TO A TROPICAL DEPRESSION

NEW INFORMATION
---------------

* CHANGES TO WATCHES AND WARNINGS:
- All watches and warnings have been canceled

* CURRENT WATCHES AND WARNINGS:
- None

* STORM INFORMATION:
- About 70 miles north of High Island TX or about 90 miles
west-northwest of Cameron LA
- 30.5N 94.6W
- Storm Intensity 35 mph
- Movement Northwest or 315 degrees at 8 mph

SITUATION OVERVIEW
------------------

Edouard has been downgraded to a Tropical Depression with the 10PM CDT
advisory. Maximum sustained winds are now estimated to be 35 mph, with
occasional tropical storm force gusts still possible through the next
couple of hours. A Wind Advisory will remain in effect through 1AM for
Tyler, Jasper, and Newton CO, as a result. The center of Edouard is
near NW Hardin CO at this time, moving NW, with the area of heaviest
rain situated north of the center. The threat for flooding rain will be
the main concern through the overnight period, as the storm continues
to weaken. A Flood Watch remains in effect for all of SE TX through
7AM.


POTENTIAL IMPACTS
-----------------

* FLOODING RAIN:

Additional impacts from flooding rain are still a concern across
interior southeast Texas. Remain well guarded against life-threatening
flood waters having further impacts of extensive potential.

Additional impacts from flooding rain are still a concern across
interior southeast Texas. Remain well guarded against life-threatening
flood waters having further impacts of limited to significant
potential.


* WIND:
Little to no additional wind impacts expected.

- Community officials are now assessing the extent of actual wind
impacts accordingly.
- Emergency work crews are restoring essential community
infrastructure as necessary.
- If you have an emergency dial 9 1 1.


Elsewhere across Southwest Louisiana and Southeast Texas, little to
no impact is anticipated.

* TORNADOES:
Additional impacts from tornadoes are still a concern across
Southwest Louisiana and Southeast Texas. Remain well braced against
tornado event having further limited impact potential.

PRECAUTIONARY/PREPAREDNESS ACTIONS
----------------------------------

* EVACUATIONS:
Follow the advice of local officials.


* OTHER PREPAREDNESS INFORMATION:

Check on your neighbors. If necessary, help them connect with their
points of contact.

Allow extra time for emergency vehicles to reach you as they navigate
road hazards.

Do not go sightseeing within impacted communities. Sightseers
interfere with the emergency work of first responders.

Be alert for any lingering wind gusts which could take down weakened
trees and/or power lines, collapse damaged structures, or cause
flying debris.


* ADDITIONAL SOURCES OF INFORMATION:
- For information on appropriate preparations see ready.gov
- For information on creating an emergency plan see getagameplan.org
- For additional disaster preparedness information see redcross.org

NEXT UPDATE
-----------

As it pertains to this event...this will be the last local statement

properties.description:
* WHAT...Snow. Total snow accumulations of 3 to 6 inches for
locations above 2,000 feet and 1 to 3 inches below 2,000 feet,
with higher amounts above pass level. Winds could gust as high
as 30 mph over Atigun Pass Tuesday night.

* WHERE...Central/Eastern Brooks Range and Eastern Arctic Coast.

* WHEN...Through Wednesday, September 2nd.

* IMPACTS...Travel could be difficult. Gusty winds could lead to
areas of blowing snow which could significantly reduce
visibility.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...A series of fronts working across the North
Slope will support moderate snow accumulations in this region.
Precipitation will remain predominantly snow in the Brooks
Range, with a rain/snow mix along the Eastern Arctic Coast on
Tuesday transitioning to all snow Tuesday night into Wednesday.
properties.instruction:

call 5 1 1 for the latest road conditions.

properties.headline: Air Quality Alert issued September 1 at 2:56PM CDT by NWS St Louis MO
properties.description:
The St. Louis Clean Air Partnership has issued an air quality alert
for the St. Louis metropolitan area from 9 AM to 8 PM CDT Wednesday.

An Orange air quality forecast means that maximum ozone
concentrations are expected to reach levels that pose a health risk.
Adverse health effects increase as air quality deteriorates. Ground-
level ozone is an air contaminant which can cause breathing
difficulties for children, older adults, as well as persons with
respiratory problems.

Reducing outdoor physical activity is recommended. If it is a
regularly scheduled work day you are urged to consider
telecommuting, carpooling, or utilizing public transit. Avoid
excessive idling and do not top off when refueling motor vehicles.
The use of gasoline-powered lawn equipment should be reduced or
postponed until late in the day.

For more information visit the St. Louis Clean Air Partnership at
http://cleanair-stlouis.com/

For current Air Quality Index (AQI) values visit
https://www.airnow.gov/
properties.note: Non-Weather Emergency Message. Not sent to IPAWS.

properties.headline: Air Quality Alert issued September 1 at 2:37PM CDT by NWS Kansas City/Pleasant Hill MO
properties.description:
The Mid-America Regional Council has issued a code Orange Air
Quality Alert for the Kansas City metropolitan area, with ground
level ozone being the primary pollutant until 7 PM CDT this evening.
Additionally, a code Orange Air Quality Alert for the Kansas City
metropolitan area is in effect Wednesday from 9 AM CDT to 7 PM CDT.

Members of sensitive groups may experience health effects.

People and businesses are urged to avoid activities which lead to
ozone formation. These activities include refueling vehicles or
topping off when refueling idling vehicles unnecessarily and using
gasoline powered lawn equipment. Positive activities include car
pooling, biking to work, delaying or combining errands, and using
water-based paints and cleaners.

When pollution levels are elevated, the Mid-America Regional Council
recommends that individuals consider limiting strenuous outdoor
physical activity to reduce the risk of adverse health effects.
People who may be especially sensitive to the effects of elevated
levels of pollutants include the very young and those with
preexisting respiratory problems such as asthma or heart disease.
Those with symptoms should consider consulting their personal
physician.

For further information, please see the Mid-America Regional Council
air quality program website at http://www.airqkc.org.

properties.description:
...RED FLAG WARNING IN EFFECT FROM NOON WEDNESDAY TO 8 PM MDT
THURSDAY DUE TO WIND AND LOW RELATIVE HUMIDITY FOR EAST BEAVERHEAD...

.Strong southwest winds will develop Wednesday as a cold front tracks
eastward and stalls along the Continental Divide. Winds will peak
each afternoon and early evening. Winds will remain elevated
Wednesday night, especially across midslopes and ridgetops, with poor
humidity recoveries.

The National Weather Service in Missoula MT has issued a Red Flag
Warning in effect from noon Wednesday to 8 PM MDT Thursday.

* AFFECTED AREA...Fire Weather Zone 111.

* TIMING...From noon Wednesday to 8 PM MDT Thursday.

* WINDS...Southwest winds 30 to 40 mph with gusts up to 50 mph.

* RELATIVE HUMIDITY...Relative Humidity between 20 to 30 percent.

* IMPACTS...Any fires that develop will spread rapidly. Outdoor
burning is not recommended.
properties.instruction:
Please advise the appropriate officials or fire crews in the field of
this Red Flag Warning.

Make and maintain your go kit. Is it ready to go? Are there any
materials you need to refresh? Visit ready.gov/kit.

A Red Flag Warning is issued when we identify weather conditions that
promote rapid spread of fire which may become life-threatening. This
does not mean there is a fire. These conditions are either occurring
now or will begin soon. It is important to have multiple ways to
receive information from authorities.
